recipes.name: Butternut Squash Soup with Cream Cheese
ingredients_raw: 6 cups peeled and cubed butternut squash

steps.text: Melt margarine in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add butternut squash, water, bouillon, marjoram, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat; reduce heat and simmer until squash is tender, about 20 minutes.
Purée squash mixture and cream cheese in a blender or food processor in batches until smooth. Return to saucepan and cook until just heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Squash Soup with Cream Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This butternut squash soup with cream cheese is blended for a smooth and creamy texture. Marjoram and cayenne pepper add even more delicious flavor.

review.reviewBody: Ok...I have to say that I tweeked this recipe big time. I used this recipe in addition to another butternut squash soup recipe. First of all, I used 2 squashes..cleaned and cut into 8 pieces..roasted them with olive oil, salt,and pepper and smashed garlic cloves for an hour in the oven..350. I then removed them from their skins..sauteed the onion and added 1 c. apple cider in addition to the chicken broth...and one peeled, chopped granny smith apple...and nutmeg, salt and pepper. I also have to say that I didnt use any of the cream cheese...the puree was perfect without..but I think I will add a small amount of 1/2 and 1/2 for a little richness. Excellent soup...thick, creamy and rewarding even if you dont use the cream cheese...way to calorie concious. Puree' in small batches in the food processor...be careful if its too hot!

I served this soup for an Oktober Fest party and everyone loved it! I roasted the sqaush on a sheet in the oven (cut in half and roast cut side down) for about 45 minutes at 375 because roasting brings out the flavor better. (Plus it is a lot easier than cutting an uncooked squash). I used butter because I never use margarine, and I added slightly more cayenne than called for. Everyone wanted the recipe. It was fabulous!

Made it with 4 cups of chicken stock, butter, and half the cream cheese (1 8oz package) and it came out delicious! Not sure if 16 ounces of cream cheese would make the soup too rich. Definitely going into our autumn/winter meal heavy rotation. 


Also, made it in my Instant Pot - put the squash in whole for 8 minutes which made peeling it a breeze, then put everything but the cream cheese in for another 8 minutes. Came out perfect.

Wonderful recipe! As suggested by other reviewers, I roasted the cubed squash (for 20 minutes at 400 degrees in my Ninja air fryer) before adding it to the soup, and, since the squash was already soft, I reduced the soup cooking time to 10 minutes. Also, as suggested by other reviewers, I used less cheese: I had about 3 oz of cream cheese and about 4 oz of laughing cow creamy cheese wedges on hand, so that’s what I used. This reduced the number of 1-cup servings to 5, with 268 calories each. The spices were perfect as written for us. It was excellent! Thanks for the recipe, which is now one of my favorites!

This recipe has officially made the “weekly” rotation. I do tweak it a bit for our family preferences and tastes. If you’re a bit more health conscious, 1/2 a cream cheese block does the trick. I always do 1 squash and adjust the “water” to the consistency we like. *Most importantly, I wanted to add that this makes an amazing pasta sauce, it gives like a Mac and cheese taste. I’ve even subbed it for Cream of Chicken Soup in a Broccoli Casserole recipe with great results. You can even add spinach or other veggies and throw it over a baked potato. The possibilities are endless.
 **Oh, I need to add that I make this in my InstantPot. I put it on PressureCook for 8 min. and then do a quick release. I then use my hand immersion blender to blend it up in the pot. Quick & Easy Healthy Cooking!!

Half the butter, quarter of the cream cheese, used 4c homemade chicken stock instead of bouillon. I roasted the butternut squash (and the seeds!) in olive oil, thyme, and turmeric for 45 min at 375 before hand- and the flavor was amazing! I only blended 2/3 of the squash, and then left the rest diced for some texture. Also added a bit of lemon juice for acidity, and then topped with goat cheese, the toasted seeds (amazing!) and a bit of parsley. Would make again with the variations!

This was a great base recipe! Like the other reviews mention, I roasted the squash after cutting it into 8 pieces for an hour at 350°F with a mixture of black pepper, Himalayan salt, freshly minced garlic, and olive oil. It comes right out of the skin with a spoon! I’m in college, so I don’t have a blender or a food processor. I just mashed the hot squash with the cream cheese using a large spoon and incorporated it into the soup after adding the broth and spices. Oh yeah! I used 3 cups of chicken broth instead of the water and chicken bouillon cubes. I also added about a pound of chicken breast tenderloins that I cubed to 1 inch pieces. I put these in with the onions to get them started. Delicious! Sprinkle with some Parmesan cheese when serving. Pairs great with some beer bread.

I roasted two squash with a head of garlic in the oven for 70 minutes after tossing with avocado oil, salt and pepper. I used my Vitamix to purée in small batches the squash along with onions that I sautéd in butter, cooked bacon, and chicken bone broth. I dumped the puréed soup into a pot. For a spicy kick, I roasted two large seeded jalapeños and purées those with some heavy cream and added that to the squash mixture. This was fantastic and really hit the spot for a warm, rich meal on a blustery cold fall day. We made some homemade sourdough bread too that we used to dip in the soup.

I roasted the butternut squash because I think it has a better flavor. In addition, I used my homemade chicken broth, it just doesn’t compare to bouillon cubes. I loosely followed the recipe, trying to get as close to the amounts as possible. I followed other reviewers’ advice and cut the cream cheese in half, just to reduce the calories. It was a wonderful meal on a cold winter’s day.

I had a carton of Trader Joe’s Miripoux….sautéed in 1/3 c butter. Added approximately 32 oz Trader Joe’s cubed Butternut Squash and aprox 3/4lb “baby” carrots. Mixed well with the miriproux then added aprox 64 oz chicken broth. Cooked until everything was soft , added 8oz cream cheese and cooked until melted. Used my stick blender until very smooth. Couldn’t help myself so. I also added about 1c half&half. So freekin’ delicious.

I love the smell of soup cooking in a slow cooker, so adapted this for crockpot cooking. Accidentally chopped too much squash (oops!), so I doubled the recipe for freezing. I just chopped and dumped everything but the cream cheese into crockpot and cooked it on low for 6 hours. Tossed the cream cheese in and used my little handheld smoothie immersion blender right in the crock till everything was smooth. It's amazing! Even my squash-hating husband liked it!

I’ve been making this for years and my family loves it. A hack I use to make it quicker and easier is to use 4 bags of frozen butternut squash cubes instead. It turns this in to a super fast recipe and it’s still delicious.
This soup is so simple, yet so flavorful! A keeper.
We thought that was great; we did use half the cream cheese, and we did add a few tablespoons of maple syrup and apple cider vinegar for flavor

I love this soup but use 2-4oz of cream cheese, depending on my mood. As others, the recipe amount is far too high for my tastes. I also frequently add some sliced roasted red pepper. I think that is a delicious addition. I've made this soup many times, it is easy and always delicious.
Been a favorite!! I've made it several times. I only use 1 pkg of cream cheese.
Best and richest butternut squash soup. I limit the cream cheese to one package (8oz) not two.
This soup is delicious but seriously needs only 2-4 oz of cream cheese - 16 oz cream cheese is WAY TOO MUCH!

Followed the recipe exactly but only used 1 block cream cheese. It was amazing! The flavor and texture was outstanding. The blender makes a big difference in the texture. Vitamix on soup setting. I was thinking about using a different recipe in a soup contest next week, but I think I have to switch to this one.

Excellent soup.... so easy to make and a proven winner time and time again. I use butter, Better than Buillion (chicken) and one cream cheese (instead of two). It's got a bit of a kick too which is unexpected. My mom often makes this with no cream cheese at all.
